card.name: Split pieces of ALL-CAPS warning words
card.fires_on: Early pieces of long medical words written in capital letters, in warning headings and label headings, such as the D in OVERDOSAGE or the H in ENHANCES. The word is not finished yet and the next piece is still to come.

modes.label: OVERDOSAGE split
modes.description: The D after OVER in the capitalised heading word OVERDOSAGE.
modes.example: KEEP THIS PRODUCT OUT OF THE REACH OF CHILDREN. IF OVER<<D>>OSAGE IS SUSPECTED, SEEK

modes.label: Capitalised warning terms
modes.description: The start or middle of capitalised clinical terms in boxed warnings, such as tumors, suicidal or fatal.
modes.example: WARNING: RISK OF THYROID C-CELL<< T>>UMORS See full prescribing information for complete

modes.label: Capitalised lab or condition terms
modes.description: A middle piece of an all-caps term such as albuminuria or immunocompromised.

card.writes: It favours short word-starting pieces like me, sh and sc, and disfavours pieces that continue a word such as osition or asion.
card.plain: It fires partway through long capitalised words in warning text, before the rest of the word appears.
